To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

switching to renewable energy can reduce greenhouse gas emissions from plastics production by 50–75%, whereas switching to corn-based feedstocks can reduce emissions by approximately 25% in the near-term.
switching to renewable energy is more effective than using renewable feedstocks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the U.S. plastics industry.

1) switching to renewable energy is the dominant near-term strategy to mitigate GHG emissions from U.S plastic production; 2) in the longer term, producing bio-based polymers from advanced feedstocks and renewable energy will further reduce emissions; 3) the most effective way to reduce emissions from plastics production is to reduce emissions in other industries, especially the power sector, and 4) the best near-term strategy for reducing plastics industry GHG emissions is to switch to renewable energy.
